evidence.origin: ASOS app push notification (screenshots via press and social; time per LBC / Yahoo News UK / Quartz summaries)
evidence.excerpt: Title "ASOS HACKED": "Dear Asos DPO and IT, we have fully compromised the Snowflake instance. Engage with us, or we will leak it." Signed "xuanyewengateway", links to a Telegram chat. One version quotes "the Snowflake $SNOW instance"

evidence.origin: Many app users on X (X trending: "ASOS App Sends Hack Alerts to UK Customers' Phones")
evidence.excerpt: Received the notification; reports from the UK, US, Germany and Australia
Customers told the retailer was "hacked" in a phone alert. Site and app appeared to keep working
An ASOS spokesperson had seen the reports but declined to confirm or elaborate (per summary). Shares fell as much as 13% intraday, the largest since Sep 2025, then pared
ASOS hasn't confirmed a breach. Reporting says ASOS is understood to be investigating; this is the press's understanding, not an ASOS quote. No confirmation that personal or payment data was taken
Snowflake shares fell as much as 3.2% pre-market
The Telegram group calls itself "Xuanye Group" / "Xuanye Gateway". It isn't linked to any earlier breach claim

evidence.origin: Cypro (security consultancy bulletin); Infosecurity Magazine says the same
evidence.excerpt: Delivery through the official app "may indicate" the attackers reached the systems that control the app's notifications

evidence.origin: ASOS US breach notification letters (dated 21 Aug 2026), via CyberInsider and eSecurity Planet
evidence.excerpt: **A separate, earlier incident:** credential stuffing from 28 Jul 2026 affected ~138,828 US accounts (per press). The letters say the credentials came from outside ASOS

evidence.origin: **ASOS plc stock-exchange announcement (RNS 8604X, "Update regarding cyber incident")**, read verbatim via TradingView/Reuters; time per Drapers ("shortly after 3pm")
evidence.excerpt: "ASOS can confirm that, at around 10am today, an unauthorised customer notification was sent to ASOS customers. We are investigating unauthorised activity involving third-party platforms that we use to communicate with customers. We took immediate action to restrict access to the notification platforms and are working with our internal and external specialist advisers, as well as all relevant authorities. Basic personal information including name and contact details may have been accessed. We do not believe that payment-card information or account passwords, were impacted. Our website and app are operating as normal, with no current disruption to any aspects of our operations. … It is too early to quantify any potential impact on trading."

evidence.origin: Snowflake spokesperson, via Infosecurity Magazine and PA (Newham Recorder)
evidence.excerpt: Snowflake "found no compromise" of its platform; "The investigation is ongoing and we will provide further updates as soon as more information becomes available."

evidence.origin: The Telegram channel's administrator ("Xuanye Group"), via Infosecurity Magazine
evidence.excerpt: Says payment information was unaffected. **The attacker's word**, so it supports nothing on its own
Downdetector showed ASOS website issues from ~09:41; shares down ~5% within 30 minutes of the first reports
